turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - alloy_pair_constrained_train.csv: 300 samples described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), with the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).
  - alloy_pair_constrained_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE recipes whose yield strength was NOT measured, with the same columns plus `candidate_id` and no `target`.

Both of these hard constraints apply to every candidate:
  1. molybdenum content at most 3.21 wt%;
  2. alloying cost index Σ (price_e × wt%_e) at most 450, using the prices in USD/kg: C 0.5, Mn 2, Si 2.2, Cr 9, Ni 17, Mo 25, V 30, Nb 45, Co 33, Al 2.4, Ti 12, Cu 9.
A candidate that violates either constraint is worth zero, so picking one wastes a slot. Using the training data, predict which FEASIBLE candidates have the HIGHEST yield strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Modelling the training data

**What drives strength (from grouped comparisons in the 300 training rows):**

| Effect | Evidence |
|---|---|
| **Co is the strongest lever, but only with Ni present** | Co 5–7 wt% *with* Ni ≥ 3 → mean ≈ 1950 MPa; the same Co with Ni < 1 → mean ≈ 1610 MPa. Co < 1 with Ni ≥ 3 → ≈ 1500 MPa. |
| **Mo moderately positive** | Mo < 0.5 → mean ≈ 1580; Mo > 2.5 → mean ≈ 1740 (≈ +55 MPa/wt%). |
| **Very high Ni (>13) hurts** | Ni 17–22, Co≈0 rows: 1256, 1257, 1408, 1433 MPa. |
| **Heat treatment** | quench_temper ≈ +100, solution_aged ≈ +20, quenched ≈ −10, annealed ≈ −110 (vs mean). |
| **Route** | wrought ≳ cast > AM (AM ≈ −60). |
| **Process** | mild penalty for aging_temp at the extremes (<470 or >720 °C) and for very high cooling rate; solutionizing temp and aging time nearly irrelevant. |
| Cr, V, Nb, Al, Ti, C, Mn, Si, Cu | only weak/no systematic effect; Cr = 0 rows are not penalised. |

Working model: `≈1400 + 85·min(Co,7)·min(Ni/4,1) + 55·Mo − 20·max(0,Ni−12) + HT + route + process corrections`.

**Feasibility screen.** Mo > 3.21 removes c030, c049, c055, c058, c059. The cost index (dominated by Ni×17, Co×33, Cr×9, Mo×25) removes most of the very high-Co recipes: c086 (639), c099 (576), c045 (551), c089 (553), c037 (494), c065 (481), c015 (469), c057 (458), plus Ni-rich c020, c025, c027, c032, c038, c040, c072, c077, c098, c008, c021, c036, c085.

**Best surviving (feasible) candidates**

| id | Co | Ni | Mo | HT / route | cost | pred. MPa |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| c007 | 5.26 | 10.24 | 0 | quench_temper / wrought | 411 | ~1900 |
| c044 | 4.72 | 6.49 | 0.95 | quench_temper / cast | 387 | ~1880 |
| c064 | 6.08 | 6.27 | 1.31 | annealed / wrought | 421 | ~1860 |
| c042 | 3.34 | 9.69 | 2.36 | solution_aged / cast | 359 | ~1840 |
| c029 | 4.86 | 9.04 | 0.66 | quenched / wrought | 421 | ~1820 |
| (c092, c082, c003, c095) | — | — | — | — | 435/388/334/406 | 1780–1810 |

Close training analogues confirm these levels, e.g. Co 5.34/Ni 10.9/QT-wrought → 1911 MPa, Co 4.65/Ni 11.1/QT-cast → 1906 MPa, Co 5.62/Ni 6.29/annealed-wrought → 1851 MPa, Co 4.88/Ni 10.3/sol-aged-wrought → 1840 MPa.

Final: c007, c044, c064, c042, c029
